description: Domain-neutral graph-native arbitration between fast defaults and scoped active cognition. Candidate evidence and confidence accumulate across epochs; relative controller reliability, expected utility, latency, effort, novelty, uncertainty, and prediction error yield a continuous System-2 weight. Exact ties are refused and near-conflict or low confidence recruit a graph-held task set. Verified outcomes update eligibility, prediction error, experience, and consolidation strength incrementally, including devaluation, extinction, and reversal, while retaining the native small-net teaching seam.

rules.name: dual_process_attach_default_policy
rules.comment: A context with no explicit policy inherits the agent's unique held default. This is wiring, not a host-selected parameter.

rules.name: dual_process_attach_affective_state
rules.comment: Use the canonical agent-held affective state; the affective-state core supplies the neutral baseline and PSI projects into the same node.

rules.name: dual_process_attach_default_task_set
rules.comment: A context without a domain-specific deliberative scope inherits the graph-held default deliberation area.

rules.name: dual_process_accumulate_candidate_evidence
rules.comment: Leaky evidence accumulation is epoch-guarded so fixed-point settlement cannot consume time repeatedly.

rules.name: dual_process_score_grounded_default
rules.comment: System 1 competition. Only fresh, grounded, reliable candidates inside an external predictive basin receive a current score. Affect adds urgency and valence-congruence terms; prior System 2 consolidation adds a learned-default bias.

rules.name: dual_process_escalate_uncertainty
rules.comment: Arousal narrows tolerated uncertainty: the same ambiguous state recruits active cognition sooner when the affective system marks it urgent.

rules.name: dual_process_escalate_instinct_conflict
rules.comment: ArgminRefusal makes an exact top-score tie a first-class incompatible-instinct signal rather than silently selecting insertion order.

rules.name: dual_process_escalate_no_grounded_default
rules.comment: An empty eligible set means every available response was stale, ungrounded, unreliable, or outside its basin. System 1 may not guess.

rules.name: dual_process_commit_unique_default
rules.comment: The ordinary path: one uniquely strongest grounded candidate becomes an explicit commitment without admitting slower cognition.

rules.name: dual_process_train_verified_outcome
rules.comment: A verified active-cognition result supplies the teaching signal for an attached small net. The collapse is queued and drained inside the native rule loop.

rules.name: dual_process_derive_controller_arbitration
rules.comment: The unique leading default and graph-held System-2 forecast yield relative net values, a continuous controller weight, and margin-derived confidence.

rules.name: dual_process_escalate_near_conflict
rules.comment: Graded conflict recruits control when more than one candidate lies within the graph-held margin of the winner.

rules.name: dual_process_scope_requested_escalation
rules.comment: Copy graph-selected task-set scopes onto the request before native admission.

rules.name: dual_process_incremental_positive_consolidation
rules.comment: Verified reward updates prediction error, experience, eligibility and bounded habit strength; one success cannot create a full habit.

rules.name: dual_process_devalue_or_extinguish_default
rules.comment: Negative, devalued, extinguished, or reversed outcomes weaken rather than erase the habit, preserving relearning history.
